entries.title: One year, two cats, and a little corner of the internet.
paragraphs: I've been running this page for a year now. I thought I'd be documenting life with Lux and Leo. What I didn't expect was how lovely it would feel to find people who are just as excited about their cats as I am.

People who understand why a photo of Leo watching the birds deserves a place on my camera roll. Why finding Lux's favourite ball is an event. Why we plan things around the cats, talk to them all day, and love them like our little babies.

There's something really nice about not having to explain any of that. I see other people building their days around the animals they love, and I feel seen. A little less weird for being this devoted to two very fluffy members of the family.

And I love how much there is to look forward to here. As soon as autumn arrives, my feed fills with films to watch, cosy corners and little seasonal traditions. Other people's excitement rubs off on me. I start noticing the season more, even if our version of an autumn activity is sitting by the window with two cats who have very important bird business to attend to.

That's what I'd like to keep in this diary: a few moments from our week, the things we're learning as cat parents, and the thoughts that don't always fit into a reel. Some weeks will be lovely. Some will involve fur on absolutely everything and a search under the sofa for one particular ball.

If you've been here for a while, thank you for making this feel like a little community. And if you've only just found us, I'm glad you're here. There's always room for someone else who wants to talk about their cats.

entries.title: Brushing their teeth is a real learning curve.
paragraphs: Last week we took Lux and Leo to the vet for their one-year vaccines and checkup. They got their shots, and everything else looked good. The one thing the vet mentioned was that their gums looked a little swollen and their teeth could use a bit more cleaning. I was surprised to hear that because I do brush their teeth a couple of times a week. I use a little cat toothbrush and chicken-flavored enzyme toothpaste, though I have to admit it is never the easiest part of our routine. They hate having their mouths handled, and I usually have to work around a fair amount of wriggling.

The vet suggested switching from the little toothbrushes to finger brushes. They make it easier to reach the teeth and gently massage the gums. He also sent us home with a zinc and vitamin C gel, with instructions to put a drop on the brush and use it while cleaning their teeth and massaging their gums. It sounded simple enough when we talked about it at the appointment, so I thought we would give it a try.

Lux was first. I quickly discovered that the gel did not want to stay on the finger brush. It sat on top like a little droplet and slid off while I was trying to get Lux settled in a position where I could reach his teeth. It took a couple of tries to get the gel on and keep it there. Lux was difficult to hold still, and the finger brush was new to him too. I can understand why he was unsure; he is a little easier for me with the old cat toothbrush.

Then it was Leo's turn, and I realized Lux had not actually been the difficult one. Leo is smaller and much more flexible, which meant he could kick and wriggle his way out of my hands in every direction. It was hard to keep him still long enough to brush, but eventually I did manage to feel his teeth and massage his gums. I think we made a little progress, even if the whole thing took a few attempts and a lot more patience than I expected.

I ordered those first toothbrushes and the toothpaste a couple of weeks before we adopted the boys. I wanted to be ready when we finally brought cats home, and when I saw that the toothbrushes had good reviews, I even ordered a second pair to keep in the cupboard. I thought I had picked the right thing and would be all set. It turns out there is always something new to learn once the cats are actually here.

That is one of the things I am learning as a first-time cat mom: caring for them means paying attention, listening when something needs to change, and being willing to try again. I may never get every little thing right the first time, but I can keep learning and make the adjustments that help them. For now, we will keep practising with the finger brushes, one wiggly attempt at a time.
